results.fact: Trailhead/approach named in itinerary+timing (Holden Village) vs. everywhere else (Phelps Creek)
results.correct_value: Itinerary follows the Phelps Creek / Spider Gap approach: ~13 mi, ~4,450 ft gain and ~1,500 ft loss to Cloudy Pass, the reverse on the way out; ~7,550 ft gain car to car
results.evidence: Elevations agree across sources: Phelps Creek trailhead ~3,500 ft, Spider Gap ~7,100 ft, Lyman Lake ~5,500 ft (a hiking guide, and a GPS-logged trip report with min 3,491 / max 7,073 ft, 6.5 mi and 1,900 ft to Spider Meadow, 1.8 mi Lower Lyman to Cloudy Pass). Distance: one trip report logs 7.2 mi to the upper Spider Meadow camps plus 4.5 mi over the gap to the north end of Lyman Lake, then 1.5-1.8 mi to the pass (~13 mi); a trail database gives 13.7 mi to Cloudy Pass; the row's own approach prose (Spider Gap 7.7 + 3.5 + 1.8) sums to 13.0, so the Cloudy Pass waypoint's 11.0 (and the partner lines built on it) was the outlier. Gains are computed from the agreed elevations and the row's own Lower Lyman (5,587) and Cloudy Pass (6,440) figures. dist_km stored the round trip (39.59 km, self-described as such in the approach prose) and is reset to the one-way figure to the summit (~14.3 mi = 23.0 km). Day hours and timing hours are left unchanged (not in dispute).

patches.expect: Most parties reach Cloudy Peak via Holden Village (Lady of the Lake ferry across Lake Chelan, then bus to the village) and hike the Railroad Creek / Hart-Lyman Lake trail up the valley. It's a long but gentle, well-graded trail past Hart Lake and Crown Point Falls to Lyman Lake, with Cloudy Pass just beyond — camp at Lyman Lake or up at the pass itself.
patches.value: Drive to the Phelps Creek Trailhead and follow Trail #1511 up the valley to Spider Meadow, then climb through upper Phelps Basin and up the permanent snowfield to Spider Gap. Drop down the north side past the Lyman Glacier and Upper Lyman Lakes to Lower Lyman Lake, then climb the meadows to Cloudy Pass — camp at Lower Lyman Lake or up at the pass itself.

results.fact: Crevasse/glacier hazard on Safety tab vs. the approach's own Spider Gap glacier crossing
results.correct_value: No glacier travel on the climb itself, but the approach crosses the permanent snowfield (former Spider Glacier) below Spider Gap both ways
results.evidence: Hiking guides and trip reports agree the Phelps Creek approach climbs a permanent snowfield, the remains of the Spider Glacier, to Spider Gap, with an axe or traction recommended and the snow dangerous when hard or refrozen; one forum thread records it as downgraded to a snowfield and raises hollowing underneath. Sources do not firmly document true crevasses, so the rewritten Safety line states the snowfield crossing and its early-season/refrozen hazard without asserting crevasses.

patches.expect: N/A - no glacier travel; the route climbs open heather and talus directly from Cloudy Pass to the summit, not the nearby Spider Glacier/snowfield
patches.value: None on the climb itself — the route climbs open heather and talus from Cloudy Pass to the summit. The approach, though, crosses the permanent snowfield left by the shrinking Spider Glacier below Spider Gap on the way in and again on the way out; treat it with care early in the season and whenever it has refrozen hard.

results.fact: NWAC forecast-zone coverage: Reports tab (climate) vs. Safety tab (avalanche)
results.correct_value: Copper Peak lies in NWAC's East Slopes Central zone
results.evidence: The official NWAC forecast-zone polygons (public avalanche.org map layer) place Copper Peak's summit coordinate inside East Slopes Central; NWAC's own zone descriptions define East Slopes Central as Lake Chelan to south of I-90 (East Slopes North is the Canadian border to Lake Chelan). The Safety line also wrongly called the route non-glaciated, which the row's own crevasse field contradicts, so the whole line is rewritten.

results.fact: Season window (Jun-Jul) vs. best_season's stated 'sweet spot' (June into August)
results.correct_value: Best window June-July; from August the glacier opens up
results.evidence: A July 2018 trip report found minimal crevasse danger mid-July and records an earlier August attempt turned back by sketchy late-season conditions on the Dark Glacier; a route summary says early season is best for the brush and that later in the year crevasses are more open and the neve icy. Both put the best window before August, matching season, pro_tips and climate.summer; best_season's own later sentence already says August-October exposes more crevasses.
